rows.street_address_1: Address Not Listed In The Dropdown
rows.additional_description_1:
Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.  The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings.  One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

 

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

Baychester Library: 2049 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475; and

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026.  Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.

Contact: Joannene Kidder, NYC DOT, 55 Water Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10041, Phone: (929) 505-1002, E-mail: ShoreRoadBridgeBX@dot.nyc.gov

Under HPD's Affordable Neighborhood Cooperative Program, occupied City-owned residential buildings are purchased by Restoring Communities Housing Development Fund Corporation (Sponsor) and then rehabilitated by a private developer selected through a request for qualifications.  Upon conveyance to the Sponsor, buildings will be managed by the private developers.  Following completion of rehabilitation, Sponsor conveys the building to a cooperative housing development fund corporation (Cooperative Corporation) formed by the buildings tenants.  The cooperative interests attributable to occupied apartments will be sold to the existing tenants for $2,500 per apartment.  The cooperative interests attributable to vacant apartments will be sold for a price affordable to families earning no more than 165% of the area median income.

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Sponsor for the nominal price of one dollar per building.  When completed, the project will provide 50 affordable cooperative dwelling units.

At the time of sale, the Sponsor will be required to sign a rental regulatory agreement with HPD containing, among other things, restrictions on rents, incomes, and assets.  When the Sponsor conveys the building to the Cooperative Corporation upon the completion of rehabilitation, the Cooperative Corporation will be required to sign a cooperative regulatory agreement with HPD containing, among other things, restrictions on sale prices, incomes, and assets as well as requirements for a flip tax and building reserve fund.

NOTICE OF PUBLIC INPUT SESSIONS

The New York City Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE) will host Public Input Sessions in all five boroughs to discuss proposed changes to the New York City Charter.  COGE is empowered to consider revisions to the Charter for presentation to the voters at the November 3, 2026 general election, or at another designated election date pursuant to law.

What are these Public Input Sessions about?

The Charter provides the structure of City government and sets out key powers of City elected officials and agencies.  After a review of the entire Charter, COGE may recommend changes intended to help City government work more efficiently and better serve all New Yorkers.

The public is invited to hear from experts, testify about any matter of importance to City government, and to suggest changes to the Charter.  You can find out more about the New York City Commission on Government Efficiency by visiting us at our website:  www.nyc.gov/COGE.

Who can give input?

These meetings are open to the public, and the public will have the opportunity to testify before members of COGE.  Any member of the public may testify about their ideas for improving the City Charter for up to three (3) minutes.  COGE will hear testimony from people who attend the meeting in person and from people who attend by Zoom.  COGE will hear testimony from individuals who appear in person before hearing testimony from those attending via Zoom.  A group, organization or institution wishing to testify shall select a single designated representative.  New Yorkers from any of the five boroughs may testify.  COGE will attempt to accommodate everyone who signs up to speak at this hearing, but if time does not permit all testimony to be heard, the public is encouraged to utilize other opportunities to testify, including by testifying at subsequent COGE public input sessions or by submitting written testimony at https://tinyurl.com/COGE2026comments.   

How do I submit written testimony?

The public may submit written testimony at https://tinyurl.com/COGE2026comments instead of or in addition to testifying live at a hearing.
